chunks.arabic_text: بِإِسْنَادِهِ عَنِ الْكُلَيْنِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنِ الزُّرَارَةِ قَالَ

translations.en: Via his chain to al-Kulayni from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar b. Udhayna from Zurara who said:

chunks.arabic_text: جَاءَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَيْرٍ اللَّيْثِيُّ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَقَالَ لَهُ: مَا تَقُولُ فِي مُتْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ؟

translations.en: Abdallah b. Umayr al-Laythi came to Abi Ja`far (peace be upon him) and said to him: what do you say about Mut`a of women?

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ: أَحَلَّهَا اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَعَلَى لِسَانِ نَبِيِّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَهِيَ حَلَالٌ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ

translations.en: He said: Allah made it Halal in His book and upon the tongue of His prophet (peace be upon him and his family) – so it is Halal up to the day of judgment.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ مِثْلُكَ يَقُولُ هَذَا وَقَدْ حَرَّمَهَا عُمَرُ وَنَهَى عَنْهَا!

translations.en: He said: O Aba Ja`far – someone like you says this while Umar forbade it and prohibited others from it!
He said: even if he had done so!

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ: وَإِنِّي أَعِيذُكَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَنْ تُحِلَّ شَيْئًا حَرَّمَهُ عُمَرُ

translations.en: He said: I seek refuge for you with Allah from permitting something which was forbidden by Umar.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ لَهُ: فَأَنْتَ عَلَى قَوْلِ صَاحِبِكَ وَ أَنَا عَلَى قَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَهَلُمَّ أَلَا أُعَيِّنُكَ أَنَّ الْقَوْلَ مَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَإِنَّ الْبَاطِلَ مَا قَالَ صَاحِبُكَ

translations.en: He [Zurara] said: so he [al-Baqir] said to him: then you are upon the verdict of your man [Umar] while I am upon the verdict of the messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) – come forth I challenge you to an imprecation [Mubahila] confirming that the truth is that which the messenger of Allah said and that what your man said is false.

chunks.arabic_text: فَأَقْبَلَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَيْرٍ فَقَالَ: يُسْرِكَ أَنْ نِسَاءُكَ وَبَنَاتُكَ وَأَخَوَاتُكَ وَبَنَاتُ عَمِّكَ يَفْعَلْنَ ذَلِكَ؟

translations.en: so Abdallah b. Umayr drew near to him and said: would it please you that your women-folk, daughters, sisters, and cousins do that?

chunks.arabic_text: فَأَعْرَضَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ حِينَ ذَكَرَ نِسَاءَهُ وَبَنَاتَ عَمِّهِ

translations.en: so Abu Ja`far (peace be upon him) turned away from him when he brought up his women-folk and cousins.

en.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia doctrine of *Naskh al-Tafsir* (abrogation of meaning) versus *Naskh al-Hukm* (abrogation of ruling), asserting that Umar’s prohibition was a human decree rather than divine abrogation. The Imam’s challenge to Abdallah ibn Umayr to invoke divine curse (*Mubahala*) underscores the authority of the Prophet’s explicit permission, while his reaction to the mention of his family illustrates the practical social considerations behind the eventual widespread acceptance of the practice.
en.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on Mut'ah (temporary marriage) and how does it differ from the Sunni view regarding Umar's prohibition?

key_terms.صَاحِب: Sahib (referring to a specific authority, here Umar)
